tasks.title: HANGS General Contracting · FY2026 Equipment and Leases Audit
tasks.description: Audit HANGS General Contracting LP's property, equipment and leases at June 30, 2026 from 11 Excel, PDF and Word files: the trial balance, the fixed asset register, the purchase invoices and signed capital expenditure requests, the scrap certificate, the equipment hours log, the policy, the rental register, the crane rental agreement, the office lease amendment and the controller's lease schedule. Roll the register forward to the trial balance, vouch every addition to its invoice and approval, test the disposal, recompute depreciation, compare every life with the policy, look for impairment indicators, and test every rental and the office lease under ASC 842. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.
tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft findings memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached
tasks.outputsPath: Outputs/HANGS General Contracting FY2026 Equipment and Leases Audit
tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and findings, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Not an audit report and no opinion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.
tasks.periodLine: FY2026: fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · property, equipment and leases testing for the CPA.

lines.text: One register life disagrees with the policy. EQ-3388, Hydraulic excavator, 45-ton (bought used), is depreciated over 60 months; Policy 4 gives heavy earthmoving and paving equipment 84. So it was fully depreciated in December 2024, yet it worked 1,420 hours this year and is being rebuilt (CAP-01). At 84 months it would still have 6 months to go: this year’s depreciation is understated $42,857.14, accumulated depreciation is overstated $21,428.57 at June 30, 2026, and $64,285.71 of that arose before this year (DEP-01). Four fully depreciated units still work; the 2012 crawler crane EQ-2740 at the policy’s own 10-year life logged 1,180 hours, a question for the life estimate (LIFE-01).

lines.text: One indicator. EQ-4022, Slipform concrete paver, logged 212 hours in the first quarter and none since; the Equipment Manager notes no paving work in the backlog, and Stillwater Equipment Brokers listed it on May 18, 2026 at $310,000.00. Its net book value is $427,800.00. If the partners are committed to the sale it is held for sale, at the lower of that and $291,400.00 after the 6% commission: a $136,400.00 write-down. If not, it is tested for recoverability with its cash flows. The CPA decides (IMP-01). No other unit sat idle for two quarters.

lines.text: Each of the 7 rentals is a lease in substance: a specific unit HGC alone directs for the term. 6 qualify for the short-term exemption Policy 8 elects: 12 months or less and no purchase option, including the month-to-month track loader either side may end on 7 days’ notice and the 12-month office trailer. One does not: R-26-02, Northline Crane Supply’s crawler crane, 36 months from September 1, 2025, which HGC may not end early. It is expensed as a rental, $185,000.00 this year, and appears nowhere on the controller’s lease schedule (LEASE-02). The office’s 2025 term, 12 months, was short-term; its new 60-month term from January 1, 2026 is not. The rentals, $304,250.00, are the rental part of account 6200, which agrees with the trial balance.

lines.text: Both are operating leases; none of the five finance lease tests is met. Title stays with the owner and neither has a purchase option. The crane’s 36 months are 30% of the 120-month class life, under 75%; its payments’ present value, $604,756.04, is 41.7% of the $1,450,000.00 replacement value, under 90%; it is not specialized. The office’s 60 months are 12.5% of a 480-month building life, and the renewal option is not reasonably certain, so the term stays 60 months. Operating leases still go on the balance sheet.

lines.text: At 6.75% a year, 0.5625% a month, the 60 payments in advance, rising 3% each January from $19,500.00 to $21,947.43, are worth $1,053,650.87 on January 1, 2026. After six payments the liability at June 30, 2026 is $970,390.27: $178,748.07 current. Straight-line, the lease costs $124,233.79 for January to June against $117,000.00 paid, so rent is understated $7,233.79 and the right-of-use asset is $963,156.48. None of it is recorded: the controller’s schedule is for the notes only, and it used a flat $19,500.00, so even the disclosure is $59,363.50 short (LEASE-01). Account 6300, $222,000.00, is six months at the 2025 rent and six at the new rent.

lines.text: The crane’s 36 payments of $18,500.00 in advance were worth $604,756.04 on September 1, 2025. Level rent paid on the first leaves the right-of-use asset equal to the liability, and the $185,000.00 expensed is the straight-line cost: income is right, the balance sheet is not (LEASE-02). events.result: Propose materiality from the year’s contract revenue, as the audit plan sets it
events.locator: Trial Balance!A8:D44; balances at June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025

events.result: Contract revenue $71,055,500.00 x 0.5% = $355,277.50, rounded down to $350,000.00. Performance materiality $262,500.00; clearly trivial $17,500.00. Property and equipment, net, is $9,035,000.00, 26 times materiality, and the year’s depreciation $1,351,000.00: every addition and every asset is tested, not a sample. Accumulated depreciation: $3,879,000.00, plus $1,236,000.00 for the year, less the scrapped truck’s $300,000.00, is $4,815,000.00, account 1555 exactly. The building rolls from $575,000.00 to $690,000.00 with no additions. Every register line foots: cost less accumulated depreciation is its net book value.

events.result: Every one of the 29 assets recomputes to the cent at its register life: cost times the months in service this year over the life, a full month in the month placed in service, never more than what was left to depreciate. EQ-3205, EQ-3460 finished depreciating during the year. The total, $1,351,000.00, is account 6600 exactly. The arithmetic is right; whether each life is right is the next test.

events.locator: Hours Log!A8:I35 and Listed for Sale!A8:F8; hours by quarter, assignments, notes and the unit listed for sale

events.result: One register life disagrees with the policy. EQ-3388, Hydraulic excavator, 45-ton (bought used), is depreciated over 60 months; Policy 4 gives heavy earthmoving and paving equipment 84. So it was fully depreciated in December 2024, yet it worked 1,420 hours this year and is being rebuilt (CAP-01). At 84 months it would still have 6 months to go: this year’s depreciation is understated $42,857.14, accumulated depreciation is overstated $21,428.57 at June 30, 2026, and $64,285.71 of that arose before this year (DEP-01). Four fully depreciated units still work; the 2012 crawler crane EQ-2740 at the policy’s own 10-year life logged 1,180 hours, a question for the life estimate (LIFE-01).

events.result: Decide which rentals are leases and test each against the short-term exemption
events.locator: Rentals!A8:I15 and 6200 Analysis!A8:B11; every rental agreement and what account 6200 holds

events.result: Each of the 7 rentals is a lease in substance: a specific unit HGC alone directs for the term. 6 qualify for the short-term exemption Policy 8 elects: 12 months or less and no purchase option, including the month-to-month track loader either side may end on 7 days’ notice and the 12-month office trailer. One does not: R-26-02, Northline Crane Supply’s crawler crane, 36 months from September 1, 2025, which HGC may not end early. It is expensed as a rental, $185,000.00 this year, and appears nowhere on the controller’s lease schedule (LEASE-02). The office’s 2025 term, 12 months, was short-term; its new 60-month term from January 1, 2026 is not. The rentals, $304,250.00, are the rental part of account 6200, which agrees with the trial balance.
events.locator: Rentals!A8:I15 and 6200 Analysis!A8:B11; every rental agreement and what account 6200 holds

events.result: Classify the office lease and the crane lease: finance or operating
events.source: 07 Leases/Northline Crane Supply rental agreement NCS-RA-2291.pdf
events.locator: PDF page 1; term, rent, cancellation, options, use and replacement value

events.result: Both are operating leases; none of the five finance lease tests is met. Title stays with the owner and neither has a purchase option. The crane’s 36 months are 30% of the 120-month class life, under 75%; its payments’ present value, $604,756.04, is 41.7% of the $1,450,000.00 replacement value, under 90%; it is not specialized. The office’s 60 months are 12.5% of a 480-month building life, and the renewal option is not reasonably certain, so the term stays 60 months. Operating leases still go on the balance sheet.
events.source: 07 Leases/Northline Crane Supply rental agreement NCS-RA-2291.pdf
events.locator: PDF page 1; term, rent, cancellation, options, use and replacement value

events.result: Recompute the office lease’s liability and right-of-use asset with its escalations
events.source: 07 Leases/Harbor Ridge office lease first amendment.pdf
events.locator: PDF page 1; the extended term and the base rent by year

events.result: At 6.75% a year, 0.5625% a month, the 60 payments in advance, rising 3% each January from $19,500.00 to $21,947.43, are worth $1,053,650.87 on January 1, 2026. After six payments the liability at June 30, 2026 is $970,390.27: $178,748.07 current. Straight-line, the lease costs $124,233.79 for January to June against $117,000.00 paid, so rent is understated $7,233.79 and the right-of-use asset is $963,156.48. None of it is recorded: the controller’s schedule is for the notes only, and it used a flat $19,500.00, so even the disclosure is $59,363.50 short (LEASE-01). Account 6300, $222,000.00, is six months at the 2025 rent and six at the new rent.
events.source: 07 Leases/Harbor Ridge office lease first amendment.pdf
events.locator: PDF page 1; the extended term and the base rent by year

events.result: Measure the crane lease that was expensed as a rental
events.source: 07 Leases/Northline Crane Supply rental agreement NCS-RA-2291.pdf
events.locator: PDF page 1; term, rent, cancellation, options, use and replacement value

events.result: The crane’s 36 payments of $18,500.00 in advance were worth $604,756.04 on September 1, 2025. Ten are paid; the liability for the other 26 is $448,826.56 at June 30, 2026, $199,035.79 of it current. Level rent paid on the first leaves the right-of-use asset equal to the liability, and the $185,000.00 expensed is the straight-line cost: income is right, the balance sheet is not (LEASE-02). With the office, $1,419,216.83 of lease liabilities and $1,411,983.04 of right-of-use assets are missing, four times materiality. Total liabilities rise by that much, which the CPA weighs against the Ferncastle covenants.
events.source: 07 Leases/Northline Crane Supply rental agreement NCS-RA-2291.pdf
events.locator: PDF page 1; term, rent, cancellation, options, use and replacement value

events.result: Crane rental is a 36-month lease (LEASE-02) · office lease not recognized (LEASE-01) · $1,419,217 of lease liabilities missing
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements overstate income by $84,310.93, 24.1% of the $350,000.00 materiality: the repair (CAP-01), the excavator’s life (DEP-01) and the office rent (LEASE-01). The balance sheet is another matter: $1,419,216.83 of lease liabilities and $1,411,983.04 of right-of-use assets are not recorded (LEASE-01, LEASE-02), 4.1 times materiality. The paver’s $136,400.00 write-down is a judgment (IMP-01), and EQ-4415 was bought without approval (APR-01). Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
